I added an "Inside top_terms.py" section to Step 3 on the same page: https://claude.ai/artifact/PC5DfnCtTvvGMd7uEXtnLm

It breaks `uv run python top_terms.py "<title>"` into six steps. Each comes from the code in `top_terms.py` and `retrieval.py` and has a short reason:

- **a. Load the collection.** It reads all 4,309 plot summaries from `data/movies.jsonl`. TF-IDF needs all of them to tell which words are rare.
- **b. Read the settings.** It loads the three Part 1 choices from `tfidf_settings.py` and checks that each value is allowed.
- **c. Build the TF-IDF matrix.** scikit-learn's `TfidfVectorizer` makes one row per movie and one column per word. A word scores higher when it appears often in this summary (TF) and in few other summaries (IDF).
- **d. Find the movie.** It tries the exact title first, then the title without its year, then any title that contains the words.
- **e. Rank its words.** It sorts that movie's row and keeps the top 15. It also counts "count here" and "movies," which show the TF part and the IDF part separately.
- **f. Print.** It prints the table, a note on the columns, the full plot summary and the settings.

One detail worth knowing: the script rebuilds the TF-IDF model from scratch every time it runs, so a change to the settings shows up on the next run.
